name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+22 district lean makes this one of the most Democratic seats in Florida
Gilbert out-raises Brown roughly four to one and holds a cash advantage
Polymarket prices Democrats near 95% to hold the open seat
About $2 million in outside spending opposing Gilbert is the main wrinkle
model.rationale: The seat's D+22 lean, Gilbert's decisive fundraising edge, and market pricing near 95% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold of this open seat. The heavy outside money attacking Gilbert signals a Republican effort, but it is unlikely to overcome a structural margin this wide.
model.watch: Any general-election polling showing a single-digit margin, or a further surge of outside spending against Gilbert, would move this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Florida's 24th District, anchored in Miami-Dade and Broward counties, is an open seat after Frederica Wilson's retirement, and it remains one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Florida at D+22. Oliver Gilbert enters the general election as a clear favorite, having raised about $1.3 million to Republican Te Mayonna Brown's roughly $313,000. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 95%.

The main complication is outside money: roughly $2 million has been spent opposing Gilbert, far more than the support on either side, a sign that Republicans see at least a sliver of an opening. With no public polling in the race, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan fundamentals, which point to a Democratic margin in the low twenties. Even a well-funded Republican effort would need an unusual shift to close a gap that large.
